content:
Sean Gallagher: kicking off SRE planning for Optimize guardrails gating rollout. need a concrete staged plan + what we do when eval runner latency spikes (since apply flow depends on it). also want initial alert thresholds so we can wire dashboards before pilot.

Rafael Mendes: +1. if we don’t have clear paging criteria we’ll end up either paging constantly or missing real issues. can we align on:
- observe-only stage duration
- soft-block vs hard-block behavior by tier
- what “latency spike” means (p95? p99?)

Aditya Rao: from product side: rollout proposal is observe-only -> soft-block (override path) -> hard-block. we can stage by tenant tier + by optimization type. biggest concern is quantization changes (highest regression risk).

Ethan Park: control plane enforcement is behind flag already. we can do per-tenant + per-route. for safe-degrade we can switch behavior if eval runner unhealthy.

Miles Thornton: we need to define “unhealthy” in a way that won’t flap. runner is async job + poll, right? what’s the budget we can tolerate before users start hitting “timeout” in UI.

Jordan Lee: enforcement path right now:
1) apply request triggers eval job
2) UI polls gating status
3) decision computed once metrics land
we have timeouts on job enqueue and job execution. we should alert on both queue delay + execution time.

Logan Wright: telemetry-wise we can emit:
- eval_job_queue_delay_ms
- eval_job_runtime_ms
- eval_job_end_to_end_ms (from apply->decision)
- eval_job_error_rate
- gating_timeout_rate
- gating_decision_rate{pass|fail|override|timeout}
label cardinality is the risk; recommend tier + optimization_type + env, but NOT tenant_id in metrics (use logs for per-tenant).

Sean Gallagher: ok, proposal for rollout stages (SRE version):
Stage 0: internal/staging dogfood, observe-only (no blocks). 1 week.
Stage 1: prod canary (5% of eligible tenants; mostly internal + 1-2 design partners), still observe-only. 1 week.
Stage 2: soft-block for quantization only (block unless override) for canary set. 1-2 weeks.
Stage 3: soft-block expanded to batching/caching/routing tweaks for canary set.
Stage 4: hard-block for quantization for all enterprise + dedicated tiers; others stay soft-block.
Stage 5: hard-block default for all Optimize applies (with controlled override path for enterprise).

Rafael Mendes: looks reasonable but we should define the canary set criteria. I suggest:
- exclude any tenant with “no prompt set / no eval coverage” (otherwise we’ll just timeout/fail)
- start with hosted-only routes first (easier to debug) then dedicated/private

Aditya Rao: agree. we also need a comms plan so CS isn’t surprised when an apply is blocked. but for SRE thread: we should lock the “what if runner slow” behavior.

Miles Thornton: what do we want the UI to do when runner latency spikes? do we show “still running” for longer? or fail fast with “timeout, try again”? and what’s the backend do — keep job running, cancel, or deprioritize?

Ethan Park: current plan is:
- UI shows “Running quality checks…”
- if end-to-end > X, UI transitions to “Timed out” with rerun option
- backend continues job unless canceled explicitly
we can add a cancel endpoint but not in first pilot.

Sean Gallagher: I’d rather have deterministic timeouts. propose:
- enqueue timeout: 10s (if queue service unavailable)
- execution timeout: 12m (hard)
- UI end-to-end timeout: 15m (soft) -> show timeout state but keep job running up to 12m execution cap

Rafael Mendes: that implies some timeouts will happen while job still running. that’s fine as long as “Refresh status” can later show result + link to artifacts.

Jordan Lee: we can return gating_run_id immediately and allow UI to fetch status later. so “timeout” is just a UX state; decision still can complete.

Nadia Rahman: do we have a target for acceptable eval overhead? we should alert before it impacts overall control plane latency / causes apply drop-offs. if p95 end-to-end goes from 3m -> 12m, that’s basically broken for user flow.

Sean Gallagher: initial alert thresholds (open to tuning):
Non-paging (warning):
- eval_job_end_to_end_ms p95 > 6m for 15m
- eval_job_queue_delay_ms p95 > 60s for 10m
- eval_job_error_rate > 2% for 10m
Paging (critical):
- eval_job_end_to_end_ms p95 > 10m for 10m
- eval_job_queue_delay_ms p95 > 180s for 10m
- gating_timeout_rate > 5% of gating attempts for 15m
- worker saturation: queue depth > 500 for 10m OR no workers reporting for 2m

Rafael Mendes: + add a “canary-specific” page? if canary is failing but rest of traffic ok, we still want to know quickly because it blocks rollout.

Miles Thornton: on mitigation playbook for latency spike, I’d put (in order):
1) flip enforcement flag to observe-only (or manual approval) for affected tiers
2) reduce concurrency / disable heavy suites (if we have suite selector by opt type)
3) temporarily increase worker pool
4) shed eval traffic to separate cluster if available
also need a clear “rollback” button for SRE oncall.

Ethan Park: we can flip per-tenant gating mode in control plane config. we already have “observe-only” and “soft-block” behind flags. manual approval mode is doable but might be post-pilot.

Logan Wright: for dashboards, I can add panels:
- end-to-end latency heatmap by optimization_type
- timeout rate
- queue depth + worker concurrency
- pass/fail/override distribution
If you want alert rules, please confirm labels so we don’t blow up cardinality.

Sean Gallagher: labels for alerts should be limited: env, tier, optimization_type. no tenant. per-tenant debugging via logs/traces (gating_run_id).

Aditya Rao: what’s the policy if runner is down completely? I know there was debate: block all applies vs allow for dedicated tiers.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE perspective: default should be “fail closed” for high-risk changes (quantization) and “fail open / manual approval” for low-risk? but product might prefer consistent behavior.

Jordan Lee: enforcement can support tier-based safe-degrade:
- enterprise/dedicated: allow apply only via override + justification when runner unhealthy
- self-serve: block apply (avoid silent regressions + support burden)
We just need to be explicit.

Sean Gallagher: +1. propose safe-degrade matrix:
Runner unhealthy =>
- quantization applies: blocked for all tiers, except enterprise can override (requires justification)
- batching/caching/routing: self-serve blocked; enterprise/dedicated can override
All events audit-logged.

Nadia Rahman: make sure overrides are visible in metrics too; otherwise we’ll think things are “passing” when they’re actually being forced through.

Logan Wright: can emit gating_decision=override + include reason=runner_unhealthy vs quality_fail. (reason label might be ok if finite set.)

Miles Thornton: + add runbook steps:
- check queue delay vs runtime (is it backlog or slow grading?)
- check if a specific suite is the culprit (e.g., rubric grader latency)
- if backlog: scale workers + pause new jobs (rate limit)
- if grader slow: switch to cached baseline / degrade to lighter suite (if supported)

Rafael Mendes: what about alert for “cache miss rate” if we rely on caching to keep latency down?

Logan Wright: we can add eval_cache_hit_rate warning if < 60% for 30m (for stable canary). but might be noisy early when cache cold.

Sean Gallagher: ok: cache alerts only after Stage 1 (once we have repeated traffic). for pilot, just dashboard.

Ethan Park: action items:
- Sean/Rafa: confirm thresholds + safe-degrade matrix
- Logan: draft dashboard + alert rules PR
- Jordan/Ethan: ensure flag flip is quick + documented for oncall
- Aditya: confirm comms + canary tenant list

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: I’ll also add “paging criteria” into the rollout checklist so we don’t go live without alerts.

Sean Gallagher: cool. I’ll summarize in the runbook doc once we lock the numbers. keep feedback coming here if anyone thinks the thresholds are too tight/loose.

Miles Thornton: one more thought: we should add an alert for “decision backlog” specifically = gating attempts waiting > 15m. that’s the user pain metric.

Logan Wright: yep can do: pending_gating_runs_count and age. will need a periodic aggregator but it’s doable.

Sean Gallagher: added. thanks all.
